source_text: Types I and II FGM, involving clitoridectomy or excision, sever nerve-rich tissues, with clinical evidence indicating long-term dyspareunia and diminished libido in up to 70% of survivors, effects absent in male counterparts.68589-5/fulltext) This outcome aligns with explicit rationales in practicing communities, where elders cite "sealing" female desire to prevent infidelity, reinforcing male authority without reciprocal controls on men.
